screens.prompt: In B6, return the commission rate for the units in B5 from the band table.

hints.syntax: =INDEX(B2:B4,MATCH(B5,A2:A4,1)): the rates, then the band position MATCH finds.
hints.func-index: INDEX turns the position into the rate sitting on that row of B2:B4.
hints.func-match: MATCH finds the band 150 falls in: the last starting point that is not above it.
hints.match-band: The band column is sorted 0, 100, 200 on purpose, so this MATCH wants 1. A 0 would look for a row that says exactly 150.
hints.require-ref: Take the units from B5 so a new figure changes the rate without an edit to the formula.
hints.value: 150 clears 100 and does not reach 200, so the second band applies and its rate in B3 is 0.04.
hints.error: Units under the first starting point have nowhere to land, and MATCH returns #N/A.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing computes
answers 2, the band position, instead of the rate that position holds
the right rate, but the band is hardcoded rather than looked up
exact match on a band table, where 150 is not itself a starting point
reads the band above the one 150 falls in
the units typed into the formula, so a new total never reaches the rate
a rate divided by zero returns #DIV/0!

docs.explain:
The band table in A2:B4 is read as ranges. 150 sits above the 100 in A3 and below the 200 in A4, so the band that applies starts on row 3 and pays 0.04. MATCH with 1 returns 2, the position of that starting point, and INDEX reads B3.

A third argument of 1 asks for the last starting point at or below the value, which assumes the column is sorted ascending. The column here runs 0, 100, 200. Set 0 instead and MATCH looks for a row that says exactly 150, finds none, and returns #N/A.

The quiet failure is a band column that has drifted out of order. A figure below the first threshold fails loudly, because MATCH finds nothing and the cell shows #N/A. Re-sort the column and check the first row before trusting a rate that looks plausible.

errors.text: The units figure is below the first starting point in A2, so no band applies and there is no rate to read.
The band column is not sorted ascending, so MATCH settles on a neighbouring row and returns its rate without an error.

docs.atWork: Commission and tax bands, where the rate changes at thresholds and the table is written smallest first.
docs.outcome: Read a rate from a sorted band table with INDEX and an approximate MATCH.

seo.title: INDEX MATCH with bands: read a rate
seo.description: MATCH with 1 finds the last band that starts at or below 150, and INDEX reads the 0.04 rate. A wrong mode returns a plausible rate from the wrong row.
